name: El Guapo
label: Dischord
lede: An accordion, an oboe, a pile of electronics and a Dischord record made in a Philadelphia living room, then a name surrendered to a Chicago band with beer-commercial money.

eras.title: A duo from Wesleyan
eras.text: El Guapo started as two college kids, Justin Moyer and Rafael Cohen, and a pile of instruments nobody else in DC was plugging in. Through the late '90s the line-up shifted, the sound got stranger, and the records came out on Resin and on the band's own Mud Memory, a long way from the Dischord house.

years.h: Justin Moyer and Rafael Cohen start El Guapo
years.p: [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]] and [[Rafael Cohen|346eee0b-4f6d-48e3-a454-ca69846a845a]] start El Guapo at Wesleyan University, according to Wikipedia. Dischord's bio places the birth in Washington, DC, in 1996, as a duo.
years.xp:
Justin Moyer, born in Philadelphia in 1977, handled vocals, bass, drums and electronics. Rafael Cohen played guitar and, eventually, oboe, an instrument you do not often find on a punk label's roster.

The line-up and the instruments would keep changing for the rest of the decade, with [[Pete Cafarella|8b976a27-0459-4c70-b6e6-6ef0277a254f]] arriving on accordion and keyboards and [[Nate Smith|b6b7fe2f-e015-4820-9577-77aa93f319a9]] on drums.

years.h: El Guapo's first 7" on Red Skies at Night
years.p: An untitled four-song single, El Guapo's first record. Dischord lists it as 4 Songs.
El Guapo's first full-length, on D.C.'s Resin label. The title set the tone: big ideas and grand abstractions, from a band still working out what it was.
El Guapo's second Resin album, from the line-up Wikipedia lists with [[Nate Smith|b6b7fe2f-e015-4820-9577-77aa93f319a9]] on drums.
A CD of improvised live pieces on El Guapo's own label, Mud Memory. The last El Guapo record before Dischord.

years.h: Nate Smith leaves; El Guapo is down to three
years.p: Drummer Nate Smith leaves before El Guapo signs to Dischord, per Wikipedia. Justin Moyer, Rafael Cohen and Pete Cafarella split the drums, bass and electronics between them.

eras.title: The Pet Sounds of DC postpunk
eras.text: On Dischord, El Guapo became the label's oddest pop band: oboe and accordion over drum machines on Super/System. They toured hard, and Fake French, cut mostly at Justin Moyer's parents' house, became their best seller.

years.p: El Guapo's Dischord debut, recorded with [[Phil Manley|726b1239-9ca1-4239-b0a0-2d64d0ec6683]] of [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]] at National Recording Studio: eighteen tracks in forty-two minutes. Dischord quotes People magazine calling it the Pet Sounds of D.C. postpunk.
years.xp:
[[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] mastered it at Silver Sonya. The tracks run from My Bird Sings to Being Boulevards.

It was a three-piece by now, each member credited with vocals and electronics on top of their main instruments. Justin Moyer covered bass and drums, Rafael Cohen guitar and oboe, Pete Cafarella accordion.

Wikipedia notes Moyer was diagnosed with epilepsy the same year.

years.h: El Guapo plays more than a hundred shows in a year
years.p: According to the band's bio, El Guapo plays over 100 shows across the United States and Europe in one year, and keeps touring through 2003 and 2004.

El Guapo's second Dischord album, recorded mostly in Justin Moyer's parents' living room outside Philadelphia and mixed by Chad Clark at Inner Ear. Dischord calls it the band's bestselling release on the label.
years.xp:
The bio says the self-recording stretched across sessions over six months. Twelve songs this time, tighter and more danceable, with titles like Space Tourist and Hollywood Crew.

One track is called Justin Destroyer, and the name stuck: Moyer would be billed as Justin Destroyer in Supersystem.

years.h: Live at Contrappunto, Perugia, Italy, November 2, 2003
yt: Live at Contrappunto, Perugia, Italy, November 2, 2003

eras.title: Losing the name
eras.text: Drummer Josh Blair arrived, Touch and Go called, and a Chicago band with corporate sponsors turned out to own the name El Guapo. El Guapo became Supersystem, made two records for Touch and Go, and called it off inside three years.

years.p: El Guapo becomes a four-piece for the first time since Nate Smith left, with Josh Blair, a drummer out of Orthrelm's hyper-technical instrumental assault.

q: You can bet that we're looking into trademarking 'Supersystem.'
years.h: A Chicago band owns the name; El Guapo becomes Supersystem
years.p: Moving to Touch and Go, El Guapo changes its name to Supersystem. The Washington City Paper reported that Touch and Go suggested it.
years.xp:
A Chicago group also called El Guapo had trademarked the name for live performance and had backing from McDonald's and Budweiser commercials. Rafael Cohen told City Paper that people like that would have the muscle to take them on. He even suggested the Chicago band play the HFStival.

Wikipedia gives a softer version: a new drummer, and a general dislike of the original name. Cohen also cited Touch and Go's co-op advertising and its distribution through Warner's ADA.

years.p: The first Supersystem album. Touch and Go pitched the band as a NY/DC quartet mixing hip-hop, electronica, punk and world music, with Justin Moyer now billed as Justin Destroyer.
Supersystem plays D.C.'s Black Cat. The photo from that night is the one Wikipedia uses for the band.
The second and final Supersystem record.
Supersystem disband, ten years after Justin Moyer and Rafael Cohen started El Guapo as a duo.

eras.title: Scattered across the dance floor
eras.text: El Guapo's members went on to dance-punk, synth-pop and, in Justin Moyer's case, the newsroom of the Washington Post. The El Guapo records went up on Bandcamp and stayed in the Dischord catalog.

years.h: Rafael Cohen joins !!!; Pete Cafarella forms [[Shy Child|78357d35-1c85-41c3-b134-37dbca97dd65]]
years.p: Rafael Cohen joins !!!, and Pete Cafarella reunites with Nate Smith in the synth-pop duo Shy Child. Josh Blair returns to Orthrelm.

years.h: Justin Moyer goes to the Washington Post
years.p: Alongside [[Edie Sedgwick|63b1219b-1910-4dfc-8ea5-6df6b2e7ac75]], his solo project first performed in drag to iPod backing, Justin Moyer starts writing for the Post, covering books, poker and city politics.
Justin Moyer's trio Light Beams wins a Washington Area Music Association award for Self Help.

years.h: Justin Moyer shares a Pulitzer at the Washington Post
years.p: Justin Moyer is part of the Washington Post team whose coverage of the January 6 Capitol attack wins the Pulitzer Prize, according to Wikipedia.
